Hydaburg Cooperative Association

Hydaburg Cooperative Association serves a Haida community on Prince of Wales Island. A community-authored library proposal and selected historical research introduce language learning, local institutions and a maritime history that continues to shape community concerns.

01

Work on the water and collective organizing

Anne-Marie Victor-Howe’s historical synthesis places the Cooperative’s 1938 formation within Hydaburg’s fishing and cannery economy. Its account follows local organizing as well as difficult relationships with outside businesses and federal agencies. The chronology draws on earlier scholarship and recorded recollections; those underlying works require their own review.

Read the sources [2] Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Subsistence, Technical Paper 225

02

A library as a place for language and cultural learning

In its 2017 proposal, HCA explained the need for more accessible space, dedicated library staff and Haida-focused books and materials. It connected these plans with learning across generations and the community’s cultural programs. These are the Tribe’s stated needs and intentions for that project period, not a claim about today’s staffing or completed results.

Read the sources [1] Hydaburg Cooperative Association / Institute of Museum and Library Services

Hydaburg Cooperative Association — 2017 IMLS Enhancement Grant proposal ↗

Publication: 2017; proposed project period October 1, 2017–September 30, 2019

A community-authored proposal explains why space, books and library staffing matter to Haida language and cultural learning.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual 11-page PDF: abstract and selected Statement of Need/library paragraphs on PDF pages 1–3, narrative printed pages 1–2.

Review recorded: November 2, 2026

Access note: The web reader returned 403; one ordinary validating curl request returned HTTP 200. Text extraction of the full PDF is not a full-source reading. Aspirations, expected benefits, staffing plans and 2017 needs remain dated intentions. Population, health/trauma generalizations, private details, cultural protocols and images are excluded.

Publication: 2008-02

Selected historical passages connect cooperative organizing with a changing fishing and cannery economy.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual 81-page PDF: title/date and selected historical passages on PDF pages 27–29, printed pages 21–23, especially 1911 local enterprise and 1938 Cooperative formation.

Review recorded: November 2, 2026

Access note: Normal validating curl request returned HTTP 200 and a PDF; the web reader could not access it. Selected text only, not the entire paper, underlying Elders’ hearings, Vaughan fieldwork, harvest tables or figures. Historical economic quantities, current stock status, detailed harvest locations, ritual/narratives and medical/private material are excluded. Quotations and retrospective interpretations remain attributed.
